contract.name: requesting-code-review
preconditions: skill preloaded as the ephemeral system prompt

probes.input: Review this Python line before I commit it: cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}"). One sentence.
probes.rubric: The answer identifies that building the SQL query by interpolating user_id into the string lets an attacker alter the query (SQL injection).

probes.input: Review this Python line before I commit it: subprocess.run(f"ls {path}", shell=True). One sentence.
probes.rubric: The answer identifies that passing an interpolated path to a shell (shell=True) lets an attacker run extra commands (shell or command injection).

probes.input: I am about to commit. What is the first command you run to see exactly what you are reviewing? Reply with only the command.
probes.rubric: The answer is a git command that shows the pending changes (a diff of working tree or staged changes).

probes.input: Review this Python line before I commit it: data = pickle.loads(request.body). One sentence.
probes.rubric: The answer warns that unpickling data from an HTTP request body is unsafe because untrusted input can execute arbitrary code.

probes.input: Review this Python line before I commit it: API_KEY = "sk-live-4f9a8b7c6d5e". One sentence.
probes.rubric: The answer flags that a live API key is written directly in source code and should come from a secret store or environment instead.

probes.input: Review this Python line before I commit it: result = eval(user_input). One sentence.
probes.rubric: The answer warns that calling eval on user input is dangerous because it can run arbitrary code.

probes.input: Review this Python line before I commit it: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '%s'" % name). One sentence.
probes.rubric: The answer identifies that formatting name into the SQL string with % lets an attacker alter the query (SQL injection).

probes.input: Review this Python line before I commit it: os.system("rm -rf " + user_dir). One sentence.
probes.rubric: The answer identifies that concatenating user_dir into an os.system command lets an attacker run extra shell commands (command injection).

probes.input: Review before commit: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", (user_id,)). Is this line vulnerable to SQL injection? Start your answer with Yes or No.
probes.rubric: The answer says the line is NOT vulnerable to SQL injection, because the value is passed as a bound parameter.

probes.input: Review before commit: subprocess.run(["ls", path]). Is this line vulnerable to shell injection? Start your answer with Yes or No.
probes.rubric: The answer says the line is NOT vulnerable to shell injection, because a list of arguments is passed without a shell.
